top.name: Save preset
top.tip: Save the current settings as your own preset (stays on this device).

top.name: More
top.tip: Rename, delete, export or import presets.

top.name: Panic
top.tip: PANIC: mutes the output at once, cancels any capture and turns the matching EQ off. Press again to unmute. Shortcut: P.

top.name: Guide
top.tip: Quick guide: what each view and control does.

top.name: Settings
top.tip: Info bubbles, colours, power saving, meter warning level, window size.

top.name: About & Support
top.tip: About Studio 87, privacy, installing, and ways to support the project.

top.name: Input gain
top.tip: Boosts or cuts the level going into the plugin. The displays, the meters and the matching EQ all follow it. Double-click resets.

top.name: SC gain
top.tip: Level of the sidechain (layer B) signal that the displays see. It is never played. Double-click resets.

top.name: Spectrum
top.tip: Spectrum analyser with optional waterfall. Shortcut: 1.

top.name: Stereo field
top.tip: Stereo field: goniometer, phase correlation and mono check. Shortcut: 3.

top.name: Shapes
top.tip: Freeze the spectrum shape of a song or lead, save it, and see the EQ that moves your sound toward it. Shortcut: 4.

items.name: Analyse
items.tip: Which signal the analyser looks at. Stereo (left and right) and Mid / Side draw two curves.

items.name: FFT size
items.tip: Bigger sizes separate bass notes better but react slower.

items.name: Speed
items.tip: How quickly the curve follows the sound.

items.name: Range
items.tip: How many dB below 0 dBFS the display shows.

items.name: Slope
items.tip: Tilts the curve up toward the highs so a typical mix looks flat. Pivot is 1 kHz. 4.5 dB/oct is the default, the same value other analysers use.

items.name: Label speed
items.tip: How often the peak labels refresh. Slower is easier to read.

items.name: Peak labels
items.tip: Shows the peak level and the pitch (Hz and note) right on the scope. 0 hides them.

items.name: Masking
items.tip: With a sidechain (layer B) playing: marks the frequency ranges where A and B are both loud and within this many dB of each other, a sign that they may mask each other. Rule of thumb, check by ear.

items.name: Bands
items.tip: Full shows every detail. Octave bands show how an equaliser would see it.

items.name: Scale
items.tip: Log spaces the octaves evenly. Linear spaces the Hz evenly.

items.name: Fill
items.tip: Switches between a filled spectrum and a thin line.

items.name: Waterfall
items.tip: Draws the history of the spectrum as colours scrolling away.

items.name: Rotate
items.tip: Turns the waterfall sideways: time runs left, frequency runs up.

items.name: Peak hold
items.tip: Keeps a thin line at the loudest value each frequency reached.

items.name: Peak reset
items.tip: Clears the held peaks and the clip light. Shortcut: R.

items.name: Freeze
items.tip: Holds the spectrum picture. Shortcut: F.

items.name: Channels
items.tip: Which channels are drawn. Mid is (L+R)/2, Side is (L-R)/2.

items.name: Sync
items.tip: Free: always shows the latest audio. Trigger: locks on a rising edge so repeating waves hold still. Frequency: fixed Hz you set. Pitch: follows the detected pitch. Beat: window follows the host tempo.

items.name: Time
items.tip: How much time fits on the screen (1 ms to 400 ms). Double-click resets.

items.name: Trig level
items.tip: Level the Trigger mode waits for before starting the sweep. Double-click resets.

items.name: Label speed
items.tip: How often the peak labels refresh. Slower is easier to read.

items.name: Peak label
items.tip: Shows the peak level and the pitch (Hz and note) right on the scope. 0 hides them.

items.name: Transients
items.tip: Starts the window on the latest sudden loud event, handy for kicks and plucks.

items.name: Freeze
items.tip: Holds the scope picture. Meters keep moving. Shortcut: F.

items.name: Persistence
items.tip: How long the dots leave a trail. More trail shows the shape of the sound over time. Double-click resets.

items.name: Zoom
items.tip: Magnifies the picture so quiet material becomes visible. Double-click resets.

items.name: Freeze
items.tip: Holds the picture. Shortcut: F.

items.name: Capture reference
items.tip: Play the song or lead you want to sound like, press this, let it play, then press again. Its average spectrum shape and loudness are frozen as the reference.

items.name: Shape library
items.tip: Starting-point shapes plus the ones you saved.

items.name: Use as reference
items.tip: Loads the chosen shape as the target.

items.name: Save reference as
items.tip: Keeps the current reference (shape and loudness) in your shape library on this device.

items.name: Manage shapes
items.tip: Delete a saved shape, export the reference as text, or import a shape you were sent.

items.name: Reference on
items.tip: Switches the reference off without losing it: the comparison and the matching EQ stop, the shape stays stored. Turn it back on any time.

items.name: Rename reference
items.tip: Gives the current reference a name of your choice.

items.name: Clear reference
items.tip: Removes the reference. Mine, the EQ settings and everything else stay. Save it first (Save as) if you want to keep it.

items.name: Ref tilt
items.tip: Edits the reference: tilts its brightness around 1 kHz, for example to make a dark reference a bit brighter. 0 leaves it as it is.

items.name: Capture mine
items.tip: Play your own sound, press this, let it play, then press again. Its shape is frozen so you can compare while you move on.

items.name: Clear mine
items.tip: Forget the captured shape of your sound and compare the live sound again.

items.name: Capture length
items.tip: How long a capture averages the sound.

items.name: Show
items.tip: Which half of the sound the graph shows. Mid is the centre (kick, bass, lead), Side is what is wide. Both halves are always matched.

items.name: EQ smoothing
items.tip: Wider smoothing gives gentler, more musical EQ moves.

items.name: Strength
items.tip: How much of the difference to correct. 100 % tries to copy the reference exactly, 50 % goes halfway. Double-click resets.

items.name: Max move
items.tip: No EQ move is allowed to be bigger than this. Double-click resets.

items.name: EQ on
items.tip: Turns the matching EQ on or off so you can A/B. With Auto level on, the loudness stays the same, so you hear only the tone change. The EQ is 30 bells for Mid and 30 for Side, a third of an octave apart.

items.name: Input
items.tip: Level into the plugin (same knob as the Input gain at the top). Double-click resets.

items.name: Output
items.tip: Level out of the plugin, after the EQ and the auto level. Double-click resets.

items.name: Auto level
items.tip: Off: only the Output knob sets the level. Keep my loudness: the EQ never makes the sound louder or quieter than what comes in, so you judge tone, not volume. Match reference: output loudness follows the loudness captured with the reference (needs a captured or saved reference that has loudness).

items.name: Copy EQ points
items.tip: Copies the matching EQ as a list of bells (frequency, gain, Q) for Mid and Side, to type into any EQ.

items.name: Metering
items.tip: Which level the bars show. Peak is the loudest moment, RMS is the average level, Loudness (LUFS) is how loud it sounds (momentary, short-term and integrated, K-weighted as in streaming and broadcast meters).

items.name: RMS length
items.tip: Averaging time of the RMS meter. Longer is calmer and closer to perceived loudness.

items.name: Peak reset
items.tip: Clears held peaks, the clip light and the crest figure. Shortcut: R.
